one_liner: Brightness Binary Feature frontal face detector in the C library ccv; about 3x faster than OpenCV's 2.x-era Haar detector, now self-deprecated.
what_it_does: ccv is a portable C computer-vision library; its BBF module detects frontal faces in grayscale images with a boosted cascade trained on 24x24 windows. The API is plain C: load a cascade with ccv_bbf_read_classifier_cascade("samples/face"), read an image as a ccv_dense_matrix_t, call ccv_bbf_detect_objects(image, &cascade, 1, ccv_bbf_default_params) and get back an array of rectangles with confidences. It is not a drop-in for OpenCV's CascadeClassifier: it uses its own cascade format and matrix type, and the repository also ships a JavaScript port (js/ccv.js, js/face.js) and a training tool (bbfcreate).
how_it_is_fast: Each weak feature compares up to 8 'positive' and 8 'negative' pixel intensities taken from three pyramid levels (full, half and quarter resolution) and fires only if every positive pixel is brighter than every negative one, exiting at the first violation; there is no integral image or variance normalization, only byte loads and compares (Brightness Binary Feature, after Abramson and Steux's YEF and Huang et al.'s rotation-invariant multiview detector). Boosted stages form an early-reject cascade, the pyramid has 6 scales per octave (interval 5) built by area resampling plus 2x downsampling, and windows are scanned on a 4-pixel grid with 4 phase offsets in accurate mode (a 2-pixel effective stride); accurate = 0 keeps one offset, which the header says is about 3 times faster.
when_to_use: Legacy or embedded frontal-face detection where a small dependency-free C detector matters more than accuracy, for example as a cheap pre-filter before a stronger model.
Grayscale images whose shorter side is at least 48 pixels with faces of 24x24 pixels or larger in roughly upright, frontal pose.
Browser or JavaScript use through the bundled js/ccv.js port, which ccv's own docs describe as the derivative that runs semi-real-time in JavaScript.
Single-threaded CPU budgets where you can trade some detection rate for speed by setting accurate = 0.
when_not_to_use: Any new project that needs accuracy: the author marks BBF deprecated ('no longer considered either fast or accurate') and on FDDB at about 250 false positives it reaches 66.27% versus 72.93% for ccv's own SCD detector; modern CNN detectors are far stronger.
Profile, rotated or small faces: the shipped cascade is frontal only, and images with a shorter side under 48 pixels return no detections at the default 24x24 size.
When you need OpenCV compatibility: it cannot load OpenCV Haar or LBP XML cascades and uses ccv's own matrix and array types.
ARM or mobile real-time targets expecting SIMD: the detection loop is scalar C, and issue #126 reports ccv's SCD detector at about 1 Hz on an iPhone 5s because its SSE2 paths lack NEON equivalents.
Projects that must stay strictly BSD without auditing the build: the default configure links GPL FFTW3 and GSL when their headers are present.

integration.form: static lib (libccv.a via ./configure and make in lib/; Bazel BUILD and Package.swift also present)
integration.dependencies: none required for BBF detection; libpng and libjpeg optional for image reading; GSL (GPL) needed only for bbfcreate training; libccv.a also compiles the bundled NNC deep-learning code, SQLite, kissfft, dSFMT/SFMT and siphash
integration.min_toolchain: C99 compiler (designated initializers); default build flags -O3 -ffast-math -march=native -msse2 on x86
integration.platforms: macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, Windows (marked with an asterisk in the README), iOS, Android, Raspberry Pi; CI on Linux x64, macOS ARM64 and Raspberry Pi 4
integration.thread_safety: not documented; detection only reads the cascade and ccv's matrix cache is thread-local (__thread), so concurrent calls on separate images appear safe from the code

gotchas: Accuracy did not reproduce for an outside user: issue #61 reports 53.82% detection with 30 false alarms on the same CMU test sets versus the documented 82.97% (12), and it was closed with no visible maintainer explanation; the speed table has the same single-run, unnamed-OpenCV harness.

Default build is not portable or license-neutral: configure adds -march=native unless --with-arch is given, compiles with -ffast-math, and links FFTW3 and GSL (both GPL) whenever their headers exist; pass --disable-fftw3 --disable-gsl to keep the binary BSD-only.

ccv_bbf_detect_objects has no input-size guard: an image whose shorter side is under 48 pixels yields zero scales and no detections at the default 24x24 size, and one under 24 pixels feeds log(0) into the pyramid-depth computation that sizes an alloca (undefined behaviour).

The trained cascade in samples/face is CC BY 4.0 (attribution required), not BSD, and BBF's windows sit on a 2-pixel grid per scale (4 pixels with accurate = 0), so box localization is coarse; the doc's validator also needs result paths hand-edited with sed before scoring.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No siblings catalogued yet; within ccv itself, SCD (scddetect with samples/face.sqlite3) is the maintained replacement, about 2x slower than BBF on the doc's example image (381 ms vs 182 ms) but about 6.7 points better on FDDB at about 250 false positives.
verified_claims_summary: doc/bbf.rst reports one `time ./bbfdetect filelist.txt ../samples/face` run over the CMU/MIT frontal test sets A, B and C converted to PNG taking 9.3 s, versus 28.0 s for an unnamed OpenCV face-detection program at default settings on the same unnamed computer (about 3.0x, derived from page data), with both timings including image decoding and output and no compiler, flags or OpenCV version stated. doc/scd.rst separately says OpenCV is about 3 times slower than BBF single-threaded and that BBF takes 182 ms versus SCD's 381 ms on addams-family.png; the matching accuracy trade on the CMU sets is 82.97% (12 false alarms) for BBF versus 86.69% (15) for OpenCV.
status_note: The repository is active (commits on 2026-10-07) but the work is in the NNC deep-learning code, none of the latest commits touch BBF, and the doc has declared BBF deprecated since libccv 0.7; the BSD-3-Clause code (lib/ccv_bbf.c plus ccv's matrix, resample and array core) remains copyable, with the face cascade under CC BY 4.0.
